claim: Let \(P_{N,\ell}\) be the compact metric graph consisting of \(N\ge2\) parallel edges of common length \(\ell>0\) joining two vertices, equipped with the standard continuity–Kirchhoff Laplacian, and let \(e\) be any edge. For the Harrell–Maltsev edgewise spectral heat envelope \(\widehat p_{P_{N,\ell}}(t,e)\), for every \(t>0\) one has the basis-independent exact identity \[\widehat p_{P_{N,\ell}}(t,e)=\frac{1}{N\ell}+\frac{2}{\ell}\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\exp\!\left(-\left(\frac{m\pi}{\ell}\right)^2t\right).\] Consequently, if \(\widehat p_e(t,e)\) denotes the decoupled Neumann-edge envelope of Harrell–Maltsev, then \[\widehat p_e(t,e)-\widehat p_{P_{N,\ell}}(t,e)=\frac{N-1}{N\ell}>0\] for every \(t>0\). Thus the strict domination conjectured in their Remark 2.1 holds on every equilateral pumpkin, with a time-independent sharp gap; all positive-frequency edgewise \(L^\infty\)-spectral weight is exactly the same as on one decoupled Neumann edge, and the entire deficit comes from the zero mode.
scientific limitations/integrity: The theorem is restricted to finite equilateral pumpkin graphs with the free standard continuity–Kirchhoff Laplacian. The proof is analytic and does not infer an infinite-dimensional statement from finite numerics; the verifier only replays finite algebra and truncated sums. No claim is made for unequal lengths, potentials, nonstandard vertex conditions, pointwise full heat kernels, or infinite graphs.
title: Exact edgewise heat-envelope domination on equilateral pumpkin quantum graphs
